newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market quiet, no sales-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market quiet, no sales-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet near midday Friday, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers reported, feedlot sources said.
Most of this week's sales were Monday and Tuesday at $70.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from last week.

Weakness early this week was attributed to slow retail beef demand and lower boxed beef prices but packers were active buyers, which spurred ideas that beef orders from retailers were heftier than expected, market sources said.
Most cattle on this week's showlists were sold by late Wednesday, cattle feeders said.

Beef sales during the week were moderately active, but packers had to lower prices to move the product, some sources noted. Movement remained strong at midday Friday, but prices also remained under pressure from large slaughter this week.
Beef prices just ahead of midday were quoted down $0.03 to $0.57 per cwt on 218 loads of fabricated cuts sold, USDA said.
Choice heavyweight cuts were quoted down $0.57 at $105.80, down $2.08 from the week-ago close.
